style.vernacular: Old walled Hausa city of mud-brick (tubali) and laterite-render compounds in earth ochre and tan, entered through a zaure gatehouse and organised around courtyards; flat or low-domed mud roofs in the old quarters, corrugated iron on newer houses; the modern city is 1-3 storey painted-render and concrete buildings behind perimeter walls, with long-span coloured metal roofs on civic and market buildings, red-brown sandy ground and sparse neem and acacia trees.
style.ornament: Hausa tambarin arewa and geometric relief patterns on gates and facades, zaure entrance halls, projecting toron-style beams and tapered mud forms on historic towers and gates, perimeter walls as the key element; unpainted brown mud gates (Marusa) alongside painted ones.
